A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BoGrape and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The rotated tables in v2 are inspectable. Ambiguous dataset attribution in v2's regression tables limits direct numerical matching, but not the overall comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original GP prediction experiments, molecular optimization results and comparisons between Limeade and random sampling.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–C report original molecular and synthetic graph optimization experiments, kernel comparisons, ablations and feasibility measurements.

M1.justification: The four kernels and GP–LCB–MIP procedure remain intact. The written binary-feature encoding changes the count-indicator domain and constraints from c in [M+1] to c in [n+1] (v1 Appendix A.4; v2 Appendix A.5), altering representable node counts. This is a local formulation revision; neighboring expressions retain inconsistent indices, and no broader implementation change is established.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates molecular prediction and design using QM7/QM9. v2 retains this coverage and adds optimization of randomly initialized GAT, GCN and GraphSAGE functions over general connected, undirected graphs with five node labels. These synthetic tasks extend evaluation beyond molecular feasibility constraints.

E2.justification: v2 adds RW, SM, WL and WLOA prediction comparators, including versions combined with the feature kernel. Existing molecular optimization comparisons gain RW-lime and WL-lime alongside Limeade and BoGrape. New synthetic comparisons evaluate Random, RW-rand, WL-rand and WL-evol; WL-evol was not an evaluated comparator in v1.

E3.justification: v2 introduces synthetic-oracle protocols and controlled experiments varying MIP limits across 60/600/1200 seconds, exploration coefficients, and baseline acquisition candidate counts from 20 to 100. It also specifies large sampling and mutation feasibility trials. The main molecular budget of 10 initial samples, 50 BO iterations and a 600-second MIP limit is retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's kernel and sampling comparisons, v2 tests the contribution of feature kernels, sensitivity to solver time and exploration settings, and whether larger candidate pools strengthen sampling baselines. Figures 5–7 and 9 examine these questions, while Appendix C.3 quantifies failures of random generation and mutation under molecular constraints.

E5.justification: The reported replication count for kernel-regression tables changes from 30 in v1 to 100 in v2. Figure 8 additionally displays distributions with medians and quartiles. BO curves retain means with 0.5 standard deviation over 10 replications; the PDFs do not establish that the original runs were simply supplemented with 70 additional runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds synthetic optimization results, additional comparator results, ablation outcomes and mutation feasibility rates, including 0.35% at N=10 and 3 successes in one million mutations at N=20. Regression values are also replaced: v1 Table 2 gives N=10 SSP RMSEs of 0.30 for QM7 and 1.20 for QM9, whereas v2 Table 3 gives one dataset-unlabeled value of 0.710. Changed replication counts and missing dataset grouping prevent interpreting this as a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: The positive-definiteness lemmas and graph-encoding bijection proofs are retained and reorganized. v2 corrects the missing-node condition from min{Au,u, Av,v}=1 in v1 Equation (7f) to zero in Equation (6f). Appendices B.3–B.4 add asymptotic analysis, including O(nL²) kernel evaluation after path-count preprocessing, without introducing a new central theorem.

C1.justification: The central shortest-path encoding and constrained acquisition-optimization contributions remain. v2 removes the explicit claim to be the first BO algorithm for general attributed graphs, states a focus on undirected graphs, and extends the abstract's empirical claim from molecular demonstrations to competitive synthetic and molecular optimization.

C2.justification: v2 substantially develops applicability and limitations in Appendix B. Its time-budget analysis qualifies v1's expectation that longer computation could improve nonlinear-kernel BO: the tested budgets mostly improve optimality gaps rather than objective values. It also discusses alternative acquisitions, scalability strategies, kernel selection and the limited suitability of generic molecular baselines, explicitly disclaiming a state-of-the-art molecular-design claim.

D1.justification: v2 adds synthetic GNN architecture details, GraKel usage, an explicit molecular feature-vector example and a statement that implementations and models accompany the supplementary materials. However, the benchmark link remains a placeholder. v1's Gurobi v11.0.0 specification and detailed 20-molecule warm-start description disappear; this establishes a documentation loss, not removal of warm starts from the implementation.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for the comparison kernels, synthetic GNN architectures, GraKel and further MIP/GNN work. It explicitly positions the Ru et al. adaptation WL-evol as a strong graph-BO comparator and softens the priority claim, while retaining the underlying MIP-based positioning. Limeade's updated publication citation refers to the same work.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and contribution presentation, consolidates the BO background and acquisition formulation, moves preliminary encoding constraints and detailed regression exposition into appendices, and gathers proofs into a dedicated subsection. It also condenses Algorithm 1 and reorganizes the experimental narrative, substantially changing how the argument is presented.

P2.justification: Figure 2 expands from four prediction panels to twelve, molecular optimization plots gain comparator curves and shared legends, and v2 adds synthetic, ablation, optimality-gap and violin displays. Regression tables are substantially restructured into rotated kernel-by-size tables, losing the previous explicit QM7/QM9 grouping. The document also adopts a different conference layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's narrow empirical validation and reliance on a sampling baseline by adding general graph benchmarks, competing BO methods and targeted robustness tests. The computational and application limitations are also better qualified. Unclear dataset attribution in the revised regression tables and incomplete access information remain weaknesses, but the stronger comparative evidence and diagnostic analyses provide a substantial overall quality gain.
